name: CAD parts and assembly models
one_line: Native and neutral geometry containers — the part, assembly and export files from which a physical thing is actually made, recognized not by a page of labelled slots but by an inter-file reference graph (an assembly naming its component files), a container-metadata property block, and a same-stem format swarm. This is the one engineering situation whose defining evidence lives between files rather than inside one, and the one whose reorganization can destroy the file's own readability by breaking stored external references. Placeholder row (J-IND, full J-DEPTH): PR-6 keeps fields empty and therefore keeps dimension_order empty; the researched order is recorded in template.why.
design_cite: Design and creative formats such as PSD, AI, SVG, Figma exports, CAD files, and 3D files should at minimum yield filename, format, dimensions or canvas properties, embedded metadata, layers or artboards where accessible, linked asset names, and preview text; unsupported proprietary formats should be recorded as indexed-but-unreadable rather than silently treated as empty.

node_test.signals_differ: Every deterministic signal on the engineering schema row is a labelled-slot relation INSIDE one document — title block, requirement rows beside verification columns, TDP manifest, change block with affected item, BOM parent/child, analysis inputs/results, verification matrix. A native CAD container has none of those: no page, no sheet, no rows, no approval slot. Its discriminating evidence is of a different kind — the linked asset names of an assembly resolving to sibling component files on disk (an inter-file edge, not an in-file slot), a container-metadata property block read by the design/creative extractor rather than a text extractor, and a same-stem multi-format swarm where one geometry appears as native, neutral and mesh. 00 licenses the mechanism directly by requiring design/CAD/3D extraction to yield `linked asset names`. No other engineering situation activates on a relation between files.
node_test.dimensions_differ: The schema's researched default is project -> design_item -> lifecycle_stage -> engineering_artifact_type. Two of those four levels are degenerate here. engineering_artifact_type takes one value across the whole corpus — a level with a single child is not a level. lifecycle_stage is almost never carried in a labelled slot inside a geometry container, so opening it would force the value to come from a filename suffix, which the schema row itself refuses (`Filename revC, final, _v7 and filesystem dates remain possible observations`). What remains is project -> design_item, where design_item is taken at the ASSEMBLY level and parts sit under their parent assembly — a value derived from a link graph rather than read from a slot. Fewer levels, differently derived.
node_test.privacy_differs: NO, and this is stated rather than inflated. Geometry is the most directly manufacturable form of a design definition and carries export-control and supplier-confidentiality exposure, but that is a difference of degree from the schema's own `potentially_sensitive`, not a difference in kind. This row does not claim the privacy leg.
node_test.why: CONNECTION's node test requires that detection signals, recommended dimensions, or privacy rules differ from the schema's default. Two of the three differ, each on its own argument, and the third is declined honestly. The row additionally carries a destination constraint no other engineering row has (see template.relocation_hazard), which is a filing rule, not a privacy rule.

fields_note: Empty by contract: a template references its schema's fields and never copies them, and PR-6 leaves the engineering schema with none declared. The legal set on any file this row recognizes is whatever R1c licenses from the engineering schema row's proposals (project, design_item, lifecycle_stage, engineering_artifact_type, revision_or_baseline) plus the universals.
proposed_fields_note: Deliberately empty. The one key this material makes tempting is a parent-assembly identifier, and minting it would duplicate `design_item` under a second spelling for a single template's convenience — the failure mode that produced thousands of private field names. The hierarchy question is parked in open_question instead. A part identifier is likewise not proposed: a short alphanumeric token is a stock code, a purchase line, an asset tag or a supplier catalogue number, and it is evidence, never a key.

deterministic: an assembly container whose extracted linked asset names resolve to sibling geometry files present on disk, together with a component/instance structure naming those same members; the resolved reference edge is the signal, and neither the extension nor a folder called CAD supplies it

a container-metadata property block carrying labelled part-number, description, material and revision slots inside a geometry file that has no sheet, no title block and no approval slot; the absence of the sheet/approval pair is half the discrimination against a released drawing

a same-stem format swarm in one directory where one geometry stem appears as a native container, a neutral exchange file and a mesh export, so that duplicate-family and version-family signals cross format boundaries rather than tracking one extension

an ASCII exchange header (a neutral-format file whose plaintext header block carries a file-name slot, a description slot and an originating-system string) followed by boundary-representation entities and no feature history
a parametric feature history or constraint/mate structure exposed by the extractor, distinguishing an authored model from a tessellated mesh that carries only triangles
an archive manifest that lists one assembly container beside several component containers sharing an identifier stem, read without extraction

a geometry file whose identifier stem is also the stem of a released sheet or a product-structure table elsewhere in the corpus; the cross-artifact stem match raises plausibility only after one of the above structures is present
parent-folder context naming an item, program or `CAD` may raise plausibility only after a reference edge or a property block is present; it never fires this row alone
needs_llm: whether a mesh file is a manufacturable definition of a designed item, a supplier catalogue component, a downloaded object to print, or a render asset, when the only evidence is triangles and a filename
whether a native container is a design item's own geometry or a purchased component imported into the corpus from a vendor catalogue
whether a surface or master model is form exploration owned by industrial design or the controlled geometry a downstream assembly and drawing derive from
whether a `.dwg` is a two-dimensional released sheet or a three-dimensional solid model saved in the same vendor container
whether a parametric script that emits geometry is principally a repository artifact, a design definition, or legally both
whether a defeatured, meshed idealisation belongs to the model it was derived from or to the analysis study that created it
never_alone: a CAD, mesh or exchange extension. 00 requires the engine to `treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning`, and `.stl` is shared by a manufacturable part, a downloaded print object, a scanned artefact and a render asset

a folder named CAD, Models, 3D, Geometry or Parts. A folder name is parent-folder context, and this row's own strongest false positive (a downloaded print object filed into `3D Prints`) satisfies it perfectly
a part-number-shaped filename stem. `91251A537.STEP` is a supplier catalogue number, not this user's design item, and the same shape is a stock code, an asset tag or an invoice reference

a revision-shaped filename token (`_RevC`, `_v7`, `_FINAL`, `_fixed`). Native models are habitually versioned by filename and by `.bak` copies; a revision property in a labelled slot is direct evidence, a suffix is not
a bounded download session. 00 states that `A session should never be treated as proof of topic`, and a downloads folder full of `.stl` files is exactly that
geometric triangles or a mesh alone. A tessellated surface is produced by CAD export, photogrammetry, sculpting, terrain data and medical imaging
an assembly-shaped filename without resolvable linked asset names. An assembly whose references cannot be resolved is an unreadable container, not proof of a design item

a company, supplier or CAD-vendor string in container metadata. The originating-system string names the authoring tool, and 00's university-name defect applies unchanged to an organization in a role slot
absence of EXIF on a viewport image. It does not prove a screenshot, and a picture of a model is not a model
a `.dwg` extension shared with a released sheet. The same container holds both; only the sheet/title-block structure discriminates

proposed_context_terms_note: PROPOSED for R6, not design. 00 states the pattern-plus-context shape for course codes only and does not list these. `external reference` and `pack and go` are listed because their correct outcome is a relocation warning, not an activation.
work_types_note: Candidate VALUES of engineering_artifact_type (or a widened canonical artifact_type) scoped to this situation, never child nodes. They are recorded because the schema row lists `CAD model` as a single value and this row's material subdivides it; that subdivision is a value list, and it is not an argument for more rows.
grouping_reasons: one assembly and the component containers its linked asset names resolve to, held together because separating them breaks the assembly's ability to open
one geometry stem across its native, neutral and mesh representations, as a duplicate-and-version family that crosses format boundaries
one design item's geometry beside the sheet, product-structure table and analysis that name the same identifier, without any of those rows losing their own facts
a configuration or variant family driven from one master container

a sparse `bracket_v7_FINAL_fixed.SLDPRT` may join an accepted assembly neighbourhood without acquiring that assembly's design_item; the graph assembles context and does not copy labels onto sparse files

template.why: Empty by binding PR-6: the engineering schema declares no destination-eligible fields, so no machine-readable order may be encoded. Subject to R1c, the researched order for this situation is project -> design_item, taken at the ASSEMBLY level, and it is deliberately SHORTER than the schema's researched default of project -> design_item -> lifecycle_stage -> engineering_artifact_type. engineering_artifact_type is dropped because it resolves to one value across this corpus and a level with one child is not a level. lifecycle_stage is dropped because a geometry container rarely carries a labelled maturity slot, so the level could only be filled from a filename suffix or a filesystem date, which the schema row explicitly refuses. Parts sit under their parent assembly for 00's parent-makes-child-intelligible reason: a component identifier is as meaningless without its assembly as Homework 3 is without its course. The user may reverse, remove, add or flatten this; it is a recommendation, not a filesystem.
template.relocation_hazard: Unique to this row and stated as a filing rule, not a privacy rule: native assemblies resolve their components by stored path and filename, so a per-file move that a user accepts can leave the assembly unable to open. This is not from 00 — it is an observed property of mainstream parametric CAD systems, marked inference. The recommendation is that any proposal touching a resolved reference set be made at the whole-set granularity rather than per file. The product policy question is raised in open_question rather than decided here.

collides_with.signal: The sharpest boundary on this row, because the two share an identifier stem by design. This row owns the geometry container the sheet is generated FROM; drawing-package owns the sheet that RELEASES it. Discriminating structure: a title block plus revision table plus approval slot plus annotated tolerances belongs to the sheet; a reference graph plus property block plus feature history and NO sheet belongs here. Fixture bytes on both sides: `BPA-210-001_Bracket.SLDPRT` and `BPA-210-001_RevC.pdf` share a stem and a directory. This row must not take the PDF because the stem matches; drawing-package must not take the SLDPRT because it carries a revision property, since a property slot is not a revision table with an approval. The `.dwg` container holds both kinds and is discriminated only by the presence of sheet structure.

Both hold three-dimensional geometry and both can be `.obj` or `.stl`. This row owns geometry whose destiny is a physical part — a units declaration, material and part-number properties, a parent assembly, a sheet or a product-structure table naming it. creative.3d-asset owns geometry whose destiny is an image or a runtime — materials, UV maps, rigs, lights and render output beside it. Fixture bytes on both sides: `hero_prop_highpoly.blend` is theirs on scene-graph evidence even in an engineering directory; an `enclosure.obj` exported for a product visual is theirs when it sits beside textures and a scene, and mine when a native parametric sibling with an item identifier sits beside it.

A downloaded supplier or standard component model looks exactly like this row's evidence: exchange format, part-number-shaped stem, sitting in a CAD directory, referenced by a real assembly. It is reference material the design uses, not the design definition it produces. Fixture bytes on both sides: `91251A537.STEP` is standards-library because the identifier belongs to a vendor catalogue and no local property block was authored; the same file becomes this row's evidence only if the user re-authored it into a design item with its own identifier and description.

An analysis idealisation is geometry too, and often carries the same stem. This row owns the as-designed geometry; simulation-analysis owns the defeatured, meshed, load-and-boundary-condition model and the study that produced it. Fixture bytes on both sides: `BPA-210-001_RevC.STEP` is mine as the design definition and is theirs only as a named input recorded inside a study; a mesh file carrying element definitions and load cards is theirs even when its stem matches mine.

Surface and master models are native geometry and are also form work. This row owns geometry that downstream assemblies, sheets or product-structure tables reference; industrial-design owns form exploration evidenced by variant studies, CMF boards and renders with no downstream reference. Fixture bytes on both sides: a `Housing_ClassA.3dm` is industrial-design when its neighbourhood is renders and colour studies, and mine when an assembly's linked asset names resolve to it. This seam is not fully settled — see open_question.

Mould, die and fixture models are CAD containers with assemblies and part numbers, and toolpath files derive from geometry. This row owns the product's own definition; tooling-fixture owns the geometry of the thing that makes the product, and the toolpath is manufacturing regardless of which model it came from. Fixture bytes on both sides: `BPA-210-001_OP20.nc` is manufacturing even though it was generated from my `.SLDPRT`; a `Core_Cavity.SLDASM` whose components are mould plates is tooling-fixture even though its structure is identical to mine.

Board and enclosure geometry are exchanged in both directions and share item identifiers. This row owns mechanical geometry; pcb-layout owns copper, stackup, netlist and fabrication outputs. Fixture bytes on both sides: a `board.step` exported for mechanical fit checking is mine when an enclosure assembly resolves it as a component, and theirs when it is a member of a fabrication package beside layer and drill outputs.

A mesh export for fabrication belongs to both worlds. This row owns the geometry as a definition; prototype-build owns the build event — machine, material lot, parameters, outcome. Fixture bytes on both sides: `bracket.stl` is mine when a native parametric sibling and an item identifier exist, and theirs when it is a member of a build record naming machine and material.

A building information model is three-dimensional, under revision, and structurally similar. Construction_property owns a model whose hierarchy is site, building and storey and whose relation is to one property; this row owns a reusable designed item. Fixture bytes on both sides: `Level-02_Structure.ifc` stays construction_property; a modular plant skid that is manufactured repeatedly is mine even when installed at one site.

also_holds_with.signal: A parametric script that emits geometry is genuinely a repository artifact and genuinely a design definition; the two claims rest on disjoint evidence (repository root and manifest on one side, item identity and downstream reference on the other). Fixture: `bracket.py` in a repository beside its exported neutral file. Restricted to the engineering schema row's declared co-activation set.
A geometry file can be the controlled definition of a design item and the named input of a knowledge-producing study at once, each independently evidenced. Neither side may infer the other's facts.

also_holds_with_note: Restricted to schemas the engineering schema row already declares as co-activations. `creative` is deliberately NOT listed: the render-asset relation is a collision, expressed against `creative.3d-asset`, and a template row must not widen its schema's co-activation edges.

falls_through_to.why: The default outcome for a geometry container that is readable but has no resolvable reference edge, no authored property block and no downstream artifact naming it — a model that is plainly technical but whose owning item cannot be established from its own evidence.
falls_through_to.design_cite: Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.

falls_through_to.why: For proprietary containers the extractor cannot open and for packed archives that cannot be inspected. 00 requires these to be recorded as indexed-but-unreadable rather than treated as empty, which is exactly the state a locked native CAD container is in.
falls_through_to.design_cite: Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.

falls_through_to.why: For a standalone exchange or catalogue geometry file with durable reference value and no assembly, project or item relation — the supplier component and the isolated neutral export.
falls_through_to.design_cite: Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.

falls_through_to.why: For viewport captures whose OCR looks like model evidence but which have no accepted project, item or assembly relationship.
falls_through_to.design_cite: Temporary Screenshots may live under Photos/Temporary Screenshots and hold screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship.

role_split_note: Empty, and the refusal is informative. The split this material most wants is the authoring role against the consuming role for the same geometry bytes — the assembly that OWNS a component versus the assembly that merely REFERENCES a purchased one. Both roles would need the same key (`design_item`) with opposite meanings, and there is no canonical producer/consumer key to split against. Minting one to solve a single template's problem is the move that produces private field names. It is recorded in `91251A537.STEP`'s must_not_conclude instead.
sensitivity_why: A neutral geometry export is by itself sufficient to have a physical part manufactured elsewhere, which makes this the most directly exfiltratable form of a design definition; supplier confidentiality and export-control exposure attach to the same files. This is a difference of degree from the engineering schema's own potentially_sensitive, not a difference in kind, and the row does not claim privacy as its node-test leg. No handling class is assigned; 00's rule that privacy policy is enforced before any model or connector receives content governs unchanged.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH NJ-CAD-1: relocation is destructive here in a way it is nowhere else — native assemblies resolve components by stored path and filename. Should cad-model files be index-and-link only and never proposed for a move; should proposals be made only at the whole resolved-reference-set granularity (recommended); or should per-file proposals be made with a warning? This is product policy, not a template's decision. NJ-CAD-2: CAD is hierarchical and the schema offers one `design_item` key. Should design_item take the top assembly for all members, with part identity searchable but not a dimension (recommended); should it be per-file, which yields one folder per part and destroys the assembly grouping; or should a parent-assembly key be minted, which this row refuses as a duplicate spelling? NJ-CAD-3: the industrial-design seam is unsettled — is a Class-A surface master this row's controlled geometry or industrial-design's form work when both neighbourhoods are present? NJ-CAD-4: does a readable-but-uncontextualised native container belong to Review Later (recommended, because it is partly understood) or to Unsupported or Encrypted (because the geometry itself is opaque even when metadata is not)?
